toolCallDetails.arguments:
{"path":"snake_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a brand-new, complete, self-contained single HTML file (this file does not exist yet — generate it from scratch) implementing a classic Snake game. Requirements:

STRUCTURE: One HTML file containing all CSS in a <style> tag and all JavaScript in a <script> tag (no external files/libraries).

GRID: Game board is a 30x30 grid, rendered on an HTML5 <canvas> (e.g. 600x600px, 20px per cell), centered on the page with a dark theme (dark background, bright grid/snake/food colors, retro monospace font for text).

GAME SCREENS (a simple state machine: 'menu' -> 'playing' -> 'gameover'):
1. START MENU screen (shown first, and shown as overlay div on top of / instead of canvas): Title "SNAKE", and three selectable game mode buttons/options:
   - "Human vs Human" (two player-controlled snakes)
   - "CPU vs Human" (one player snake, one CPU snake)
   - "CPU vs CPU" (both snakes controlled by AI, spectator mode)
   Player can select a mode by clicking a button or pressing 1/2/3, then press Enter/Space (or click a Start button) to begin. Show brief control instructions on the menu (Arrow keys for Player 1, WASD for Player 2 when applicable).
2. PLAYING screen: canvas visible, HUD showing current score(s) at the top (Player/CPU labels and score numbers, e.g. "Player: 12   CPU: 8" or "Player 1: 12   Player 2: 8"), live gameplay.
3. GAME OVER screen: overlay showing "GAME OVER", the winner (or "Draw"), final score(s), and text "Press ENTER to play again" / "Press ESC for menu".

SNAKE MECHANICS:
- Continuous movement in one of 4 directions (up/down/left/right) on a fixed game-loop tick (e.g. every 100-120ms via setInterval or requestAnimationFrame with accumulator), NOT moving on every keypress.
- Snake cannot instantly reverse into itself (ignore a direction input that is the exact opposite of current direction).
- Snake grows by one segment each time it eats food (food is a single randomly-placed cell not currently occupied by any snake body).
- After eating food, spawn a new food cell at a random empty grid position.
- Collisions end the game for the colliding snake: hitting a wall (grid boundary), hitting its own body, or hitting the other snake's body (when 2 snakes are in play). Handle simultaneous head-on collisions and head-to-head collisions between the two snakes as a draw/tie ending for both.
- When only one snake remains alive (in 2-snake modes) it wins immediately; in single relevant scenarios keep rules consistent. Game ends -> go to GAME OVER screen.

MODES (support all 3, selectable from menu):
- Human vs Human: Snake 1 controlled with Arrow keys, Snake 2 controlled with W/A/S/D keys. Both start on opposite sides of the board moving toward the center, different colors (e.g. green and blue).
- CPU vs Human: Snake 1 (player) controlled with Arrow keys (or WASD), Snake 2 controlled entirely by AI.
- CPU vs CPU: both snakes controlled entirely by AI (no player input affects movement); this is a spectator/demo mode.

CPU AI: Implement a reasonably smart AI for CPU-controlled snakes that automatically searches for the nearest food using a pathfinding/greedy approach: use BFS (breadth-first search) over the grid from the CPU snake's head to the food position avoiding cells occupied by any snake body and walls, to compute the next-step direction along the shortest safe path. If no path to food is found, fall back to a safe-move heuristic that picks any adjacent cell that is not a wall/body collision and, ideally, has the most open space (simple flood-fill/available-space count) to survive longer, preferring not to trap itself. Recompute the path every tick (or when needed) since the board changes as snakes move.

CONTROLS:
- Arrow keys: move Snake 1 (Player 1) — used in all modes where snake 1 is human-controlled.
- W/A/S/D keys: move Snake 2 (Player 2) — used only in Human vs Human mode.
- Enter or Space: start game from menu / restart game from game-over screen.
- Escape: return to menu from game-over screen (or during play to abort back to menu).
- 1/2/3 keys on the menu: quickly select game mode.
- Prevent default browser scrolling behavior for arrow keys/space during gameplay (event.preventDefault()).

SCORING: Track and display each snake's score (number of food items eaten) live during gameplay in a HUD area above or over the canvas, updated in real time. On game over, show final scores and the winner.

RESTART: From the game-over screen, pressing Enter/Space (or clicking a "Play Again" button) immediately restarts a new game in the same mode; pressing Escape (or clicking "Main Menu" button) returns to the start menu where a new mode can be chosen.

CODE QUALITY: Well-structured, commented vanilla JavaScript (no frameworks), organized into clear functions/objects (e.g. a Snake class/factory, a Food module, an AI/pathfinding module, a render function, an update/tick function, an input handler, and a state-machine/game-controller). Clean, readable CSS with a polished retro/arcade look (nice colors, box shadows/glow on the canvas, centered layout, readable fonts). Make sure the whole thing runs correctly by simply opening the HTML file in a browser, with zero external dependencies."}
